html_en:
The agent economy is arriving faster than anyone expected — from Andrej Karpathy's vision of neural computing displacing classical code to Aaron Levie's blueprint for how enterprise software will adapt to headless AI usage. Meanwhile, the infrastructure race is heating up as platforms scramble to build for a world where machines, not humans, are the primary users of their products.

The Neural Native Economy Takes Shape

Karpathy laid out his most compelling vision yet for the post-classical computing era in a lengthy thread summarizing his Sequoia Ascent talk. Beyond the obvious productivity gains, he sees three transformative categories emerging:
"menugen: an app that can be fully engulfed by LLMs, with no classical code needed: input an image, output an image and an LLM can natively do the thing."
The second category challenges our entire software distribution model:
"install .md skills instead of install .sh scripts. Why create a complex Software 1.0 bash script for e.g. installing a piece of software if you can write the installation out in words and say 'just show this to your LLM'."
Most intriguingly, Karpathy points to knowledge bases as proof of functionality that
"was *impossible* with classical code because it's computation over unstructured data (knowledge) from arbitrary sources and in arbitrary formats."
This isn't just about speeding up existing workflows — it's about entirely new categories of possible software that couldn't exist before.

Enterprise Software's Headless Future

Aaron Levie provided perhaps the most detailed roadmap yet for how enterprise software will adapt to agent-driven usage in a comprehensive thread. His central thesis:
"As agents become the biggest users of software, then all software has to be available in a headless fashion. Agents won't be using your UI, they'll be talking to your APIs."
Levie outlines a three-tier pricing evolution: - **Human seats** remain but must include generous API allowances for agent usage - **Agent seats** for stateful AI workers, though pricing remains tricky since one customer might use one agent while another uses thousands - **Consumption pricing** for headless usage that exceeds seat allowances The growth implications are staggering:
"the use-cases for agents operating on data in these systems will dramatically exceed what people do with their data and tools today."

The Agent Development Stack Matures

The tooling ecosystem is rapidly professionalizing. Anthropic released Claude Code's desktop redesign built explicitly for parallel agent orchestration, while Catherine Wu announced Claude Security in public beta — a vulnerability scanner that's already caught issues existing tools missed. Sam Altman highlighted a "big upgrade for codex today" encouraging users to
"try it for non-coding computer work."
The pivot from coding-specific to general computer use reflects the broader expansion happening across agent platforms. Peter Steinberger of OpenClaw reported significant improvements to group chat functionality, noting "I changed how agents talk there, it IS SO GOOD NOW." The focus on collaborative workflows suggests agents are moving beyond individual productivity toward team coordination.

Real-World Deployment Stories

swyx shared how his team uses agents to run AI Engineer serving ~1 million developers monthly, calling it a "Tiny Team" approach. His prediction:
"'coding agents breaking containment' is the breakout theme of the year. this is the year all knowledge workers, not just coders, get AGI-pilled."
Meanwhile, Amjad Masad demonstrated Replit's commitment to eating their own dog food, sharing a "Prompt ➡️ LLC" workflow that generated a complete business entity from natural language.

Infrastructure Scramble

The race to become agent-native is creating both opportunities and growing pains. Peter Yang highlighted a common frustration: "Shit breaks half the time when I tell my bot to update itself." Self-modifying systems remain fragile, but the appetite for them suggests the potential rewards justify the current instability. Nikunj captured the strategic imperative:
"Be in the path of these models using you - or you'll simply cease to exist. First, terminal. Then, computer use. Soon, the entire OS."
The cybersecurity implications are profound. Aditya Agarwal observed that "We're going through a critical inflection point for cybersecurity in real time," as both attackers and defenders gain AI capabilities simultaneously.

The Deeper Questions

Beneath the tactical developments, fundamental questions about human-AI collaboration are emerging. Amanda Askell pushed back against internet speculation about her work, noting "it's weird to experience it first hand" how confidently people write fiction about AI researchers. Her frustration hints at the broader challenge of maintaining authentic discourse as AI capabilities advance. ryolu offered a philosophical perspective on system design, arguing that "'no opinion' is itself a strong one" and that true flexibility comes from
"strong opinion held in cohesion – not about one ideal workflow, but about which concepts are fundamental."
As we hurtle toward this agent-mediated future, the winners may be those who best understand that building for AI users isn't just a technical challenge — it's a fundamental rethinking of what software can be.
html_zh:
从编程助手到完全自主的代理，AI工具正在重新定义知识工作的边界。今天的AI生态系统展现出一个清晰的趋势：我们正在从单一任务的自动化转向多任务并行的智能编排。

代理突破"容器边界"：知识工作的全面重构

Andrej Karpathy 在 Sequoia Ascent 2026 的炉边谈话中，提出了一个重要观点：大语言模型的意义远超加速现有工作流程。

"我试图推动的第一个主题是，LLM不仅仅是加速以前存在的东西（比如编程）。三个新视野的例子：1) menugen：一个完全可以被LLM吞噬的应用，不需要传统代码：输入图像，输出图像，LLM可以原生地处理这件事。2) 安装.md技能而不是安装.sh脚本。为什么要为安装软件创建复杂的Software 1.0 bash脚本，如果你可以用文字写出安装过程并说'把这个给你的LLM看'。LLM是英语的高级解释器，可以智能地针对你的设置安装，内联调试一切等等。3) LLM知识库作为传统代码根本不可能实现的东西的例子。"

swyx 呼应了这一观点，在播客中提到 "编程代理突破容器"是今年的突破主题：

"这是所有知识工作者，不仅仅是程序员，都会被AGI化的一年。"

这种转变的具体体现是多任务并行处理。Claude Code 发布了桌面版重设计，专门为并行代理工作流程优化，支持同时运行多个会话，让开发者能够"在一个仓库中启动重构，在另一个仓库中修复bug，在第三个仓库中编写测试"。

安全：AI时代的双刃剑

随着AI代理能力的增强，安全问题变得更加复杂和紧迫。Anthropic 推出了Claude Security 公开测试版，集成到 Claude Code 网页版中，能够识别和修复代码漏洞。

Aditya Agarwal 与 Palo Alto Networks CEO 的播客中强调了这个转折点：

"攻击者有AI。防御者也有AI。网络安全有了新的形态：AI既是威胁，也是唯一可行的解决方案。"

令人担忧的是，Amanda Askell 发现自己成为了网络虚假信息的目标，抱怨："我越来越多地看到关于我的内容，断言非常自信但完全是编造的。"这揭示了AI时代信息真实性面临的挑战。

软件商业模式的根本性转变

Box CEO Aaron Levie 发布了一系列深思熟虑的观点，探讨代理成为软件主要用户后的商业模式变革：

"当代理成为软件最大的用户时，所有软件都必须以无头模式提供。代理不会使用你的UI，它们会与你的API对话。"

他预测了三种定价模式的演进：

1. 传统座位许可将保留给人类用户，但需要包含API使用额度

2. 代理可能需要"座位"进行状态化工作，但定价方式会完全不同

3. 消费模式将主导超出座位分配的无头使用场景

Replit CEO Amjad Masad 展示了这种转变的早期迹象，演示了"提示词 ➡️ 有限责任公司"的流程，展现了AI如何能够处理复杂的商业流程。

个人AI助手的成熟

个人AI代理工具正在快速成熟。OpenClaw 的创始人宣布了群聊功能的重大改进：

"如果你在群聊中尝试了OpenClaw但得到了混合结果，你必须再试一次。我改变了代理在群聊中的对话方式，现在非常好用了。"

Dan Shipper 展示了使用 Codex + Chronicle 作为专注力追踪器的实验，而Ryan 将 Cursor SDK 集成到他的 ryOS 中，实现了通过对话直接编辑操作系统的功能。

Sam Altman 宣布了Codex 的重大升级："今天Codex有重大升级！试试用它做非编程的计算机工作。"

设计哲学：无观点即强观点

Ryan 发表了一篇深刻的设计哲学思考：

"人们把'有观点的'和'通用目的'当作对立面。它们不是。当你决定什么概念存在，什么可见，什么组合，什么扩展，什么隐藏——你已经表达了一种世界观。'无观点'本身就是一个强观点。"

他论述了构建通用系统的核心原则："为通用性而构建意味着表达非常具体的观点：核心概念应该是少数的、持久的、灵活的。"这种设计哲学在当前AI工具的快速发展中显得尤为重要。

随着AI代理从简单的任务助手演进为复杂的知识工作编排者，我们正在见证一个根本性的范式转变。正如Karpathy所说，我们要么在数据分布内"飞行"，要么在"丛林中用砍刀开路"。成功的关键是理解这种新范式的边界和可能性。
